text: this is finally painting correctly! alright sweet, now one thing about this i want to ask and then another thing before we take this anywhere is, so for painting, is possible to make it more optimistic? this is working but i can still feel some delay on a very high quality model -- expected, but im just wondering if we have the most optimal live edit possible or if we can do better. and then we have part of this but gpt also gave me a great idea with it, but currently when importing a model, we had a quality slider. it was to try and handle the models im loading right now lol. but, for the actual game, i still want this since i dont want the 400k tris model i just want its general shape, any way you can show me a live quality slider? and then gpt said we can use this quality slider for baking in LoD for render distance which is smart as hell
resolution: Delivered both asks. PAINT LATENCY: made the paint upload incremental — the atlas is now the source of truth (a paint writes straight to its texel) and only the dirty ROW BAND is re-uploaded each frame (model_paint.consumeDirtyRows -> a partial writeTexture), instead of re-pushing the whole ~1.6MB texture every stroke; removes per-stroke upload cost on high-tri models. QUALITY SLIDER: new mesh_import.decimateExpanded clusters vertices onto a grid^3 lattice (Zig sibling of importMesh.ts decimateSoup) to collapse a 400k-tri scan to its general shape live; the load door retains the full-res source and __model_set_quality(grid) re-decimates from it and swaps the resident + paint target under a quality-specific key (only key+count cross the bridge). Cart gets a Quality slider + live tri count — verified tree 4,612 -> 316 tris with the shape intact, and single-face paint still renders through the incremental path. Also answered the optimization question (the two levers are incremental upload, done, and edit-at-reduced-res via the slider; a BVH for full-res picking is the further step) and framed GPT's LoD-bake as the slider's natural payoff. Shipped on 88bf9c123; the follow-on stash-overflow fix from scrubbing landed on 08884edd5 (req_2137).
